ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening at onboarding, before incorporation, and on an ongoing basis: verify all beneficial owners, directors, authorized signatories, and counterparties against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, New Zealand sanctions made under the Russia Sanctions Act 2022, the Terrorism Suppression Act 2002 designation list, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, and any other domestic financial sanctions list administered by the New Zealand Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade. Identify domestic and foreign Politically Exposed Persons, their family members, and close associates, and apply enhanced due diligence when a match, adverse media, high-risk jurisdiction, or unexplained wealth indicator arises. Independently verify source of funds and source of wealth before incorporation, document every screening decision, retain evidence of false-positive rationalization, and flag all confirmed hits to the applicable AML/CFT supervisor (Reserve Bank of New Zealand, Financial Markets Authority, or Department of Internal Affairs) in accordance with section 43 of the AML/CFT Act.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: New Zealand Companies Office Online Companies Register and Name Availability Search (companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in English and/or Maori script, may include diacritical marks, and must be Romanized if transliterated from non-Latin scripts such as Chinese characters. The Registrar applies a four-tier naming test: (1) availability and absence of confusing similarity, (2) permissible script and character set, (3) sensitive or prohibited token approval, and (4) required legal-ending suffix, namely Limited or Ltd, for a New Zealand company.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant receives a written decision stating the statutory ground. The applicant may file a written reconsideration request to the New Zealand Companies Office within 10 working days, attaching the original reservation reference, corrected name, consent letters from any affected statutory body, and evidence distinguishing the name from prior registered names. If the Registrar maintains the rejection, the applicant may file a judicial review application in the New Zealand High Court under the Judicial Review Procedure Act 2016, in accordance with the prescribed time limits and filing fees. During any appeal, the applicant may simultaneously apply for one renewal of the name reservation for a further 20 working days to preserve priority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not per se unlawful under the Companies Act 1993, but the registered office must be a physical street address in New Zealand at which legal process can be served; a commercial mailbox or PO Box alone is prohibited. For an automated dropshipping business, the Inland Revenue Department and New Zealand banks generally reject a virtual-office-only arrangement for GST registration and merchant facility approval unless the company demonstrates substantive operational presence, such as a dedicated local director, physical inventory or warehouse access, active business banking, and complete records. If used, the virtual office must include a physical serviceable address, nameplate availability, and mail-forwarding, and cannot be used to hide beneficial ownership or evade compliance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced physical inspection by Inland Revenue or the Companies Office: (1) physical street address displayed and accessible during business hours; (2) company share register, UBO register, board minutes, and constitutional documents available or producible within 24 hours; (3) accounting and GST records consistent with reported turnover; (4) evidence of payment-provider agreements and dropshipping supply chain; (5) presence or availability of directors and staff. Quantified risk: low, below 10% annual probability, for a fully compliant office with substantive records; high, above 40% annual probability, for a virtual-only registered office with no physical substance, inconsistent GST filings, or no local director.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 1993 (NZ), ss 10-21 (incorporation), ss 22-26 (company names), ss 27-29 (constitution), s 31 (registered office), ss 87-89 (directors), s 153 (board resolutions); Financial Reporting Act 2013; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, ss 5 and 14-18 (reporting entities and customer due diligence); Tax Administration Act 1994; Income Tax Act 2007 (offshore income and non-resident-controlled company exemption rules)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: New Zealand Companies Office, an operational business unit of the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), head office located in Wellington, New Zealand; online filing via the Companies Register (https://companies-register.companiesoffice.govt.nz)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of a Company (online prescribed form) filed under section 12 of the Companies Act 1993; certificate of incorporation issued under section 21; New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) automatically issued upon registration
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up or authorised capital is prescribed by the Companies Act 1993 (NZ); the company must allot and issue at least one share at incorporation. No escrow or capital-holding account is mandated. For the International Company (Tax-Exempt Zone) structure, issued shares must be held by non-resident shareholders and working capital is typically provided by non-resident shareholder loans; the company must not carry on business in New Zealand in order to preserve the exempt treatment.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE SOLE DIRECTOR OF [COMPANY NAME] (the 'Company'), PASSED PURSUANT TO THE COMPANIES ACT 1993 (NEW ZEALAND) AND THE COMPANY'S CONSTITUTION. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED that the Company allots and issues one fully paid Ordinary Share in the capital of the Company to the subscriber shareholder at par, and that the amount subscribed is credited to the Company's stated capital, such share being held by a non-resident shareholder in furtherance of the Company's International Company (Tax-Exempt Zone) status. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED that the registered office of the Company be fixed at [Registered Office Address, New Zealand], that the address for service be maintained at the same location, and that the Registrar of Companies be notified of these addresses in accordance with section 31 of the Companies Act 1993. 3. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED that [Director Name] be and is hereby appointed as sole director of the Company; that [Secretary Name] be appointed as company secretary (if applicable); and that [Compliance Officer Name] be appointed as principal AML/CFT compliance officer, each to hold office until resignation, removal, or replacement by subsequent board resolution. 4. ADMINISTRATION: RESOLVED that the directors be and are hereby authorised to execute all incorporation filings, banking mandates, and payment gateway agreements necessary to give effect to the foregoing resolutions, including registration of the Company for tax, AML/CFT compliance, and the issuance of transaction instruments.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Companies Register online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an electronic company name search under sections 22 to 23 of the Companies Act 1993 to confirm the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to any existing registered name, and is not prohibited, misleading, or offensive. Submit a name reservation application through the Companies Register portal; reservation protects the name for 20 working days and is recommended before finalising the incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name
Company name search result printout from the Companies Register confirming no conflict
Declaration by applicant confirming compliance with sections 22-23 Companies Act 1993
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is queried or refused, the applicant may submit an alternative name electronically, request a written reconsideration of the reservation decision, or apply to the Companies Office for a formal name review; where a name is rejected as misleading, the applicant may supply supporting business-description documents or select a wholly new distinguishing name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Constitution and Shareholders' Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial director and founding shareholder, advised by company legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the company constitution pursuant to sections 27 to 29 of the Companies Act 1993, prescribing share class rights, board powers, conflict-of-interest rules, share transfer restrictions, and a statement that the Company is constituted as an International Company engaged exclusively in non-resident / offshore automated dropshipping activities. Execute a written shareholders' and subscription agreement recording the allotment, non-resident beneficial ownership, and tax-exempt intentions, and have the initial director sign the consent-to-act form.
required_dossiers: Company constitution
Shareholders' and share subscription agreement
Consent to act as director of each first director
Written declaration of non-resident ownership status
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any constitutional deficiency may be cured by a special resolution under section 32 of the Companies Act 1993; prior to first allotment the constitution may be amended or revoked by unanimous shareholder resolution, and legal counsel may issue a side letter to reconcile inconsistencies in the subscription agreement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office incorporation portal (Companies Register)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online Application for Incorporation of a Company under section 12 of the Companies Act 1993. Enter the approved or reserved company name, the registered office address, the address for service, the share allotment particulars, and the full legal name and identification details of each director and shareholder. Attach the executed consent-to-act forms and the adopted constitution, submit the application, and pay the prescribed fee by electronic card or POLi.
required_dossiers: Completed Application for Incorporation online form
Consent to act as director for each proposed director
Registered office address and address for service confirmation
Adopted constitution (where applicable)
Payment of the prescribed incorporation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is returned or rejected under section 18 for non-compliance, review the Registrar's query notice, rectify the deficient particulars (e.g., invalid address, incomplete director consent, or inconsistent share details), and re-submit the corrected application; if a certificate is ultimately refused, the applicant may seek judicial review in the High Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Receipt of Certificate of Incorporation and NZBN Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and the New Zealand Business Number (NZBN) register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon successful registration, the Registrar will issue a certificate of incorporation under section 21 of the Companies Act 1993 and the company will be automatically enrolled in the NZBN registry. Verify the incorporation number, the NZBN, and all register entries through the Companies Register, then download certified electronic copies for banking, tax, and payment gateway onboarding.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation (electronic copy)
Companies Register extract
NZBN confirmation letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate or register entries contain clerical errors, file a notice of correction with the Companies Office; any outstanding statutory particulars, such as missing director identification, must be remedied within 20 working days to avoid penalty or involuntary removal from the register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Tax-Exempt Status Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD / Te Tari Taake) via the myIR online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Company for a New Zealand IRD number using the incorporation details; apply for GST registration only if the Company anticipates a domestic New Zealand taxable activity; and seek confirmation of the non-resident / offshore income tax exemption by proving management and control, and all substantive trading activity, occur outside New Zealand. Submit the certificate of incorporation, director identification, and supporting declarations, and request a binding ruling if the tax position is complex.
required_dossiers: IRD registration form (IR596 or myIR online application)
Certificate of incorporation and Companies Register extract
Director and shareholder identification information
Tax residence declaration of the Company (management and control test)
Business activity description (ISIC 4791 automated dropshipping)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the IRD queries the structure, respond within 10 working days with the tax residence declaration, evidence of offshore management and control, and financial statements; the Company may apply for a binding ruling under sections 90A to 91 of the Tax Administration Act 1994 or issue an objection to any adverse assessment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: AML/CFT Reporting Entity Registration and Compliance Programme
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Internal Affairs (DIA) AML/CFT Group, with the Financial Markets Authority (FMA) as co-supervisor for certain payment-related activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Company as an AML/CFT reporting entity under the Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2009, given the medium-risk enhanced profile of automated dropshipping payment flows routed through Stripe and PayPal. Appoint a senior officer as AML/CFT compliance officer, adopt a risk-based AML/CFT programme covering customer due diligence, screening, and transaction monitoring, and apply enhanced due diligence to any intermediary payout providers.
required_dossiers: AML/CFT compliance programme document
Business risk assessment reflecting the Medium_Risk_Enhanced rating
AML/CFT compliance officer appointment letter
Customer due diligence records for the beneficial owner and payment intermediaries
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the compliance programme is rejected or suspended by the supervisor, engage an approved AML/CFT consultant, revise the programme within the specified remediation period, and, if a penalty is proposed, exercise the rights of reply and judicial review under the AML/CFT Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Banking and Payment Rails Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered New Zealand banks (e.g., ANZ Bank New Zealand, Bank of New Zealand, ASB Bank, Kiwibank) and regulated payment service providers (Stripe, PayPal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a non-resident corporate bank account in NZD and USD presenting the certificate of incorporation, constitution, director identification, AML/CFT registration, and source-of-funds evidence. Complete the bank's KYC and foreign-ownership questionnaires, then apply to Stripe and PayPal for merchant accounts using the legal company name, NZBN, and registered office address; configure settlement to the corporate bank account and document the beneficial ownership trail for enhanced underwriting.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation and Companies Register extract
Company constitution
Certified copies of passports of directors and ultimate beneficial owners
AML/CFT reporting entity registration certificate
Proof of registered office or physical address
Business model description and projected transaction volumes for payment gateway underwriting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the primary bank or payment partner declines, apply to alternative regulated non-bank financial institutions, reloadable e-money issuers, or a second-tier New Zealand bank; for Stripe or PayPal, submit enhanced due diligence information, a detailed website and fulfilment-process description, and independent references to mitigate the elevated risk classification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Registers, Governance Records, and First Annual Return Diarisation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: New Zealand Companies Office and the company's board of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of incorporation, establish the statutory share register and director register, record the first share allotment, and retain minutes of all board resolutions. File the first annual return before the 30th working day following the first anniversary of incorporation, and maintain a register of ultimate holding company interests if the shareholder is a corporate entity or a trust. Ensure continuing compliance with the Companies Act 1993, including notification of any registered-office or director changes.
required_dossiers: Share register under section 84 Companies Act 1993
Director register under section 88 Companies Act 1993
Initial board minutes and resolutions
Annual return confirmation (due within 12 months of incorporation)
Register of ultimate holding company interests (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the first annual return is flagged or filed late, submit the outstanding filing online immediately and apply to the Registrar for a late-filing penalty waiver providing a reasonable explanation; any register inaccuracies may be corrected retroactively by a memorandum of correction signed by the director.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No statutory industrial licensing authority is triggered for pure automated dropshipping with no physical warehouse, factory, or distribution point in New Zealand. If the Company later establishes a physical facility, the competent authorities are the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE), the New Zealand Environmental Protection Authority (EPA), WorkSafe New Zealand, and the relevant territorial authority acting under the Resource Management Act 1991 and the Building Act 2004.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required for ISIC 4791 (Retail Sale via Automated Dropshipping Networks) under New Zealand legislation. The Company may optionally obtain a voluntary 'Trusted Business' or merchant-bureau accreditation, and may register for New Zealand Trade and Enterprise (NZTE) digital export recognition to improve payment gateway and banking risk outcomes.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: New Zealand Environmental Protection Authority (EPA), together with the relevant regional council or territorial authority under the Resource Management Act 1991
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Registration-only for a paperless, home-office or virtual registered-office dropshipping model; a Full Environmental Impact Assessment (Category 3) and resource consent would be triggered only upon construction or operation of a warehouse, distribution centre, packaging plant, or other physical facility classified as a controlled or discretionary activity under the operative district plan.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not engaged for the current virtual operations. If a physical New Zealand fulfilment centre is later established, the Company must comply with the National Environmental Standards for Air Quality (NES-AQ) 2004 for particulate matter and volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions, municipal trade-waste discharge limits under the applicable regional plan for wastewater, and the Waste Minimisation Act 2008 for packaging and cardboard waste, including any product stewardship obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for the current non-physical automated dropshipping platform. Should the Company open premises in New Zealand, it must obtain: (i) a fire safety certificate and emergency egress approval under sections 65 to 70 of the Fire and Emergency New Zealand Act 2017; (ii) structural load inspection and a Code Compliance Certificate (CCC) under the Building Act 2004 building consent regime; and (iii) workplace health and safety clearance from WorkSafe New Zealand under the Health and Safety at Work Act 2015, including signage, electrical inspection, and racking or packing-station safety verification.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Inland Revenue Department (IRD) of New Zealand; online taxpayer portal myIR (https://services.ird.govt.nz/myir/).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated entity, including a Cook Islands International Company, that carries on a taxable activity in New Zealand, derives New Zealand-sourced income, or is required to register for New Zealand GST must apply to the Commissioner of Inland Revenue for an IRD number. Non-resident companies apply using the prescribed non-resident company registration form (typically IR742) supported by the certificate of incorporation, registered office address, director and shareholder details, and any New Zealand business address. Applications may be lodged through myIR or by paper. The IRD number is issued once registration is accepted. Where a non-resident company has a fixed place of business in New Zealand or central management and control is exercised in New Zealand, it may become resident and registrable for income tax purposes; otherwise it is registered as a non-resident company and taxed only on New Zealand-sourced income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone — a Cook Islands International Company is outside the New Zealand income tax base unless made resident under domestic law by central management and control being exercised in New Zealand or by deriving New Zealand-sourced income through a fixed establishment. As a non-resident entity, it is subject to New Zealand income tax on New Zealand-sourced income only, and the profits of a genuine offshore international company are not within the New Zealand taxing net.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: New Zealand does not operate a US-style check-the-box entity classification regime. Relevant statutory elections include: (a) voluntary GST registration where turnover is below the NZD 60,000 compulsory threshold; (b) GST grouping election for closely related companies under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985; (c) transitional resident tax election for eligible new residents under section 220 of the Income Tax Act 2007; and (d) application of New Zealand's hybrid and branch mismatch rules (Income Tax Act 2007 subparts FH and FE), which may recharacterise payments or deny deductions to counteract hybrid mismatch outcomes. There is no statutory election to create a New Zealand 'tax exempt zone' for a foreign international company; its tax-exempt status derives from non-residence and the territorial scope of New Zealand taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax (GST) — a value added tax imposed under the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NZD 60,000 — compulsory GST registration applies to a person carrying on a taxable activity in New Zealand where the value of supplies in any 12-month period exceeds or is likely to exceed NZD 60,000. Non-resident suppliers of remote services, digital goods, or goods delivered via automated dropshipping models are also required to register under the non-resident supplier registration rules once supplies to New Zealand consumers exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: New Zealand does not operate a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or continuous transaction control regime. E-invoicing is voluntary and supported through the New Zealand Peppol network. GST returns are filed electronically through myIR, but invoice-level data is not transmitted to the Inland Revenue Department on a transaction-by-transaction basis and no digital stamping of invoices is required. For exported goods, supporting documentation such as customs export declarations and transport documentation must be retained to substantiate zero-rating.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for (a) goods supplied by a GST-registered person that are exported from New Zealand by the supplier or on the supplier's behalf, provided the supplier has ownership or possession of the goods at the time of supply and the goods are exported within the statutory timeframe (generally within 28 days of the time of supply, or under a contractual obligation to export); (b) services supplied to a non-resident who is outside New Zealand when the services are performed, provided the services are not supplied directly in connection with New Zealand land or movable property and are not performed while the recipient of the supply is in New Zealand; and (c) certain international transport and freight services. For automated dropshipping operations, zero-rating on the New Zealand-registered operator requires either physical export of goods from New Zealand or valid offshore services treatment under section 11A of the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (New Zealand Customs Service electronic export entry / TID)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing export from New Zealand
Commercial Invoice and purchase order relating to the supply
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank statement showing foreign currency settlement and receipt of export proceeds
Proof of physical export within the statutory 28-day timeframe (e.g. customs movement records and carrier evidence)
Any agency or dropshipping agreement demonstrating that the New Zealand supplier is the principal exporter and has ownership or possession of the goods at the time of supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Commissioner of Inland Revenue may disallow zero-rating and assess GST where documentary or substantive conditions are not satisfied. Consequences include: additional GST at 15% on the original supply value, use-of-money interest, late payment penalties, shortfall penalties under the Tax Administration Act 1994 (up to 150% of the tax shortfall for evasion, and up to 40% for substantial understatement without taking reasonable care), and criminal prosecution in fraudulent cases with fines and imprisonment. Where an exporter fails to repatriate funds or cannot substantiate export within the statutory period, the zero-rating is retrospectively clawed back and the supplier becomes liable for the full GST amount plus penalties and interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Te Pūtea Matua) acts as the monetary authority for New Zealand and, on a de facto basis, for the Cook Islands, whose licensed financial institutions use the New Zealand dollar as legal tender and settle through Reserve Bank clearing systems; the Cook Islands Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) is the licensing and AML/CFT supervisor for the CK_IC's registered agent and any Cook Islands licensed bank, and the FSC administers the International Companies Act regime under which the CK_IC is incorporated.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: New Zealand operates a fully liberalised free-floating exchange rate regime with complete current-account and capital-account convertibility; the Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1984 and no Reserve Bank approval or exchange licence is required for any cross-border transfer, dividend, profit remittance, or debt repayment. The New Zealand dollar (NZD) is a globally deliverable currency with an extremely liquid spot and forward market. No restriction applies to a non-resident tax-exempt International Company (CK_IC) wishing to repatriate profits to shareholders, provided the entity does not derive New Zealand-sourced income and does not create a permanent establishment in New Zealand. Two compliance caveats apply: (a) the Overseas Investment Act 2005 requires consent only where the non-resident acquires 'sensitive land' or 'significant business assets' located in New Zealand, which is not the case in a borderless automated dropshipping operation; and (b) the Goods and Services Tax Act 1985, effective 1 December 2019, requires a non-resident supplier of low-value goods (each item NZD 1,000 or less) to New Zealand consumers to register, collect, and remit 15% NZ GST once its New Zealand low-value-goods supplies exceed NZD 60,000 in a 12-month period; failure to collect GST is a treasury sanction that can be triggered by the Inland Revenue Department. Profit remittance of the post-GST margin is fully convertible with zero statutory withholding where the distribution is made by the tax-exempt IC out of its non-New Zealand-sourced trading income.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no export proceeds surrender rules in New Zealand: no statutory surrender ratio, no mandatory repatriation timeline, and no forced conversion of foreign currency into NZD. Exporters and automated e-commerce operators may retain 100% of foreign currency receipts in onshore foreign-currency accounts or offshore accounts indefinitely; may convert to NZD at any time through a licensed dealer; and may settle intercompany or supplier balances out of such accounts without Reserve Bank notification. The only administrative obligations are statistical, i.e., the banks' Balance of Payments reporting to the Reserve Bank and the Inland Revenue Department's exchange-of-information rules. The CK_IC's effective mandatory conversion ratio is zero percent and the statutory surrender period is indefinite or none.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 25 working days after the anniversary of incorporation (annual return date).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing infringement fee NZD 50; continued non-compliance may result in strike-off proceedings under section 318 of the Companies Act 1993, with directors exposed to personal fines.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (if not exempt from filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: New Zealand Companies Office (Registrar of Companies)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the company's balance date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file may incur fines up to NZD 10,000 and further enforcement action leading to strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a standard 31 March balance date, due 7 July; for a non-standard balance date, due on the 7th day of the fourth month following the balance date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of NZD 250, plus accruing use-of-money interest and a 1% per month late payment penalty; criminal sanctions available for wilful non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit is compulsory if the company exceeds at least two of the following thresholds: (a) total assets NZD 30 million; (b) total revenue NZD 60 million; (c) 50 full-time equivalent employees. Smaller companies are exempt from audit unless required by their shareholders or a regulatory order.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: New Zealand IFRS (Tier 1/Tier 2) for reporting entities under the Financial Reporting Act 2013; small companies may use the simplified NZ Accounting Standards for Small Entities (NZ ASR). Non-resident companies may elect to report under IFRS where permitted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: New Zealand law does not impose a separate annual UBO declaration. The Annual Return to the Companies Office serves as the year-end confirmation of shareholding and directorship. Any share transfers during the year must be notified on Form CO/16 within 20 working days, and director changes within 10 working days.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$150–300 per annum for registered office/agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$5,000–15,000 for a typical small-to-mid-sized company audit; nil if audit-exempt

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for the tax-exempt International Company under the Cook Islands International Companies Act 1981-2020; 28% New Zealand company rate applies if the International Company becomes New Zealand tax-resident or derives New Zealand-source income through a fixed establishment.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full statutory income tax exemption for International Companies (no income tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty, or estate duty); annual government fee in lieu of tax; New Zealand R&D Tax Incentive (15% refundable credit) and imputation credits apply only where New Zealand-resident taxable nexus is established.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: New Zealand Inland Revenue IR4 Company Tax Return lodged electronically via the myIR Secure Online Services portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due by the 7th day of the 7th month after the balance date (e.g., 7 July for a standard 31 March balance date); residual terminal tax due 7 April of the following calendar year; provisional tax instalments due 28 August, 15 January and 7 May under the standard payment date cycle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income from all sources before expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax-exempt International Company: report zero unless New Zealand-source income arises; attach the International Company tax-exempt status certificate and registered agent confirmation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting net profit or loss before tax as per the financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile exempt offshore income to zero taxable profit; provide a reconciliation note if any New Zealand-source gross income is present.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses brought forward from prior years and applied against current-year taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not claimable by the non-resident exempt International Company absent New Zealand taxable income; New Zealand-resident companies must satisfy the 49% shareholder continuity requirement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resident withholding tax, imputation credits, and foreign non-resident withholding tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim double tax agreement credits only when New Zealand-source income was earned and foreign tax was paid; attach Inland Revenue Form IR290 and the foreign Tax Residency Certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: automatic late filing penalty of NZ$50 per month up to NZ$500; late payment penalty of 1% per month on the unpaid tax; use-of-money interest at the prescribed quarterly rate (approximately 7.09% to 9.09% per annum).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cook Islands International Company Annual Return and Government Fee Schedule (lodged through the licensed Registered Agent to the Financial Supervisory Commission / Registrar of International Companies)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on the anniversary of incorporation; annual government fee assessed by reference to authorised share capital and payable by 31 December under administrative practice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Licensed registered agent confirmation of the registered office, director register, and shareholder register.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident beneficial ownership details must be disclosed to the registered agent for AML/CFT record-keeping; no tax return is filed on exempt offshore income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tiered government fee calculated on authorised share capital; payment receipt attached.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No declaration of profits or taxable income is required for the exempt International Company; timely fee payment maintains good standing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late-payment interest of 10% per annum; deregistration and striking-off after approximately 90 days of default; licensed agent sanctions for non-compliant filings.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on distributions by the tax-exempt International Company; once New Zealand-resident company status is triggered, dividend withholding operates on an imputed 28% basis for residents, and non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) applies at 30% domestic / 15% treaty-reduced rates on dividends paid by a New Zealand-resident company.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Complete New Zealand Inland Revenue Form IR290 (Certificate of Residence) and obtain an official Tax Residency Certificate from the treaty partner jurisdiction; submit via myIR before payment to secure reduced or zero NRWT rates; for Cook Islands International Company distributions no DTA relief is required because the distribution is statutorily exempt at 0%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: New Zealand domestic NRWT: royalties 15% and interest 15%; the Approved Issuer Levy (AIL) of 2% may replace NRWT on qualifying interest; treaty rates commonly reduce royalties to 5%-10% and interest to 0%-10% depending on the double tax agreement partner (e.g., the Australia-New Zealand protocol permits 0% interest on qualifying trans-Tasman related-party lending).

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: New Zealand imposes no codified statutory dollar threshold for Local File / Master File documentation; Inland Revenue requires contemporaneous arm's length documentation for cross-border associated-party transactions, with a practical compliance focus above NZ$10 million aggregate; Country-by-Country reporting applies to New Zealand-resident groups with consolidated group revenue of at least NZ$1.2 billion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Cook Islands International Companies Act mandates a local registered office and licensed registered agent but imposes no formal Economic Substance Regulation comparable to the UAE ESR; however, New Zealand's Controlled Foreign Company (CFC) and Foreign Investment Fund (FIF) attribution rules scrutinise the substance and location of central management and control - central management and control exercised from New Zealand triggers New Zealand taxation and displaces the tax-exempt status.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Corporate Tax Evasion (New Zealand Tax Administration Act 1994)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A New Zealand tax-resident beneficial owner uses the tax-exempt Cook Islands International Company as an opaque wrapper for automated dropshipping profits sourced from New Zealand customers, without attributing CFC/FIF income and without disclosing the arrangement to Inland Revenue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Shortfall penalty for evasion of 150% of the tax shortfall under section 141E TAA, plus use-of-money interest; criminal prosecution under section 143B TAA with imprisonment of up to 5 years; the arrangement is void under section BG 1 of the Income Tax Act 2007.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate face joint and several personal liability for the company tax shortfall under section 149A TAA; disqualification orders by the New Zealand Companies Office; civil recovery, travel enforcement orders, and imprisonment of up to 5 years for aiding evasion.
